   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {
    "id": "XhOKjEQHUFid"
   },
   "source": [
    "## 1. What Is A Tensor"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "Tabular data is commonly represented in rows and columns, allowing us to easily access, analyze, and manipulate the information.\n",
    "We will encounter various tabular data structures.\n",
    "- A **scalar** is the simplest form, representing a single numerical value, such as 5 or 3.14.\n",
    "- A **vector** is a one-dimensional array of numbers, representing a sequence of values or a point in space, often visualized as a row or column of numbers.\n",
    "- A **matrix** is a two-dimensional arrangement of numbers, consisting of multiple rows and columns.\n",
    "- A **tensor** have three or more axes, making it suitable for representing complex data like images, videos, or multi-dimensional scientific data."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 3,
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "data": {
      "image/png": "",
      "text/plain": [
       "<IPython.core.display.Image object>"
      ]
     },
     "metadata": {
      "image/png": {
       "width": 1240
      }
     },
     "output_type": "display_data"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "from IPython.display import Image, display\n",
    "display(Image(\"../images/data/varied-data-structures.png\", width=1240))"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "This becomes more complicated because we need to carefully keep track of these different data structures and understand how they relate to one another.\n",
    "In machine learning and deep learning frames, the concept of **tensor is generalized to unify all these structures (scalars, vectors, rows, and matrices) under a single, consistent framework**.\n",
    "\n",
    "By treating data as tensors, we can handle simple values, one-dimensional sequences, two-dimensional tables, and even higher-dimensional data in a systematic way.\n",
    "- A 2D tensor has the shape (rows, columns), such as a matrix of size 28×28 representing a grayscale image with 28×28 pixels.\n",
    "- A 3D tensor has the shape (height, width, channels), such as a color image of 28×28 pixels with RGB channels (here, channels = 3).\n",
    "- A 4D tensor has the shape (batch_size, height, width, channels), representing a dataset containing multiple color images.\n",
    "- A 5D tensor has the shape (batch_size, time_steps, height, width, channels), such as a batch of 10 video clips, each consisting of 16 frames of 64×64 RGB images.\n",
    "- A 6D tensor has the shape (batch_size, time_steps, depth, height, width, channels), used for 3D medical images (like MRI scans) over time: 5 patients, each with 10 time points, each scan of size 64×64×32 voxels, with 1 channel per voxel."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 4,
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "data": {
      "image/png": "",
      "text/plain": [

      ]
     },
     "metadata": {
      "image/png": {
       "width": 1024
      }
     },
     "output_type": "display_data"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "display(Image(\"../images/data/generalized-tensor.png\", width=1024))"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {
    "id": "nR9mkPpZUJjt"
   },
   "source": [
    "**Tensor** vs **ndarray**\n",
    "- Tensor is similar to the fundamental object in Numpy called ndarray\n",
    "- ndarray is defined as an n-dimensional homogeneous array of fixed-size items\n",
    "\n",
    "**Advantages of Tensor**\n",
    "- Tensor operations are performed significantly faster using GPUs\n",
    "- Tensors can be stored and manipulated at scale using distributed processing on multi GPUs and GPUs and across multiple servers\n",
    "- Tensors keep track of the graph of computations that created them\n",
    "- Tensors are much more than a special sort of multi-dimensional arrays\n",
    "- Interactions with each other such that transforming the tensors as a whole means that each tensor follows a particular transformation rule\n"
   ]
  },
  {

   "metadata": {

   "source": [
    "torch.manual_seed(123456) # to keep data reproduciable\n",
    "\n",
    "# generate values from a uniform distribution on the interval [0, 1)\n",

    "\n",
    "# `torch.randperm(n)` to create a tensor with a random permutation of integers\n",
    "a_tensor = torch.randperm(10)\n",
    "print(f'a_tensor = {a_tensor} and its tensor size = {a_tensor.size()}\\n')"
   ]

  {
   "cell_type": "code",

    "executionInfo": {

     "timestamp": 1749255469630,
     "user": {

    },
    "id": "_cQJse5Pf5yx",
    "outputId": "4890e02b-a777-456e-a185-de4e42a2f648"
   },
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "# types for numbers in pytorch\n",
    "# torch.int8, torch.int16, torch.int32, torch.int64, torch.float16, torch.float32, torch.float64\n",
    "\n",
    "a_tensor_int = torch.tensor([1,2,3,4,5])\n",
    "print(f'a_tensor_int = {a_tensor_int} and its tensor dtype = {a_tensor_int.dtype}\\n')\n",
    "\n",
    "b_tensor_flt = torch.tensor([1,2,3,4,5], dtype=torch.float) # can use `float64`\n",
    "print(f'b_tensor_flt = {b_tensor_flt} and its tensor dtype = {b_tensor_flt.dtype}\\n')\n",
    "\n",
    "# data type conversion\n",
    "print('------- data type conversion (two methods) -------\\n')\n",
    "\n",
    "a_tensor_flt1 = a_tensor_int.float()\n",
    "print(f'a_tensor_flt1 = {a_tensor_flt1} and its tensor dtype = {a_tensor_flt1.dtype}\\n')\n",
    "\n",
    "a_tensor_flt1 = a_tensor_int.to(torch.float64) # or .to(dtype=torch.double)\n",
    "print(f'a_tensor_flt1 = {a_tensor_flt1} and its tensor dtype = {a_tensor_flt1.dtype}\\n')"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "<div class='alert alert-info'>\n",
    "\n",
    ":::{note}\n",
    "**More attributes for tensors**\n",
    "- `x.layout`, it indicates how a tensor is laid out in memory\n",
    "- `x.device`, it indicates a tensor’s device location (*e.g.*, CPU or GPU\n",
    "memory) (will be discussed at 5th section below)\n",
    "- `x.requires_grad`, it is a Boolean attribute that indicates whether tensor\n",
    "keeps track of graph computations\n",
    "\t- `x.grad`, it contains actual gradients if `requires_grad` is `True`\n",
    "\t- `x.grad_fn`, it stores graph computation function used if `requires_grad` is `True`\n",
    "- `x.s_cuda`, `x.is_sparse`, `x.is_quantized`, `x.is_leaf`, `x.is_mkldnn`, they are Boolean attributes that indicate whether tensor meets certain conditions\n",
    "\n",
    "**Remember that when accessing object attributes, you do not include parentheses `()` like you would with a class method (*e.g.*, use `x.shape`, not` x.shape()`)**\n",
    ":::\n",
    "</div>"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {
    "id": "KoG4GgknmRy_"
   },
   "source": [
    "## 4. Tensor Operations"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {

   "source": [
    "torch.manual_seed(123456)\n",
    "\n",
    "a_tensor = torch.rand(5,5)\n",
    "print(f'a_tensor = {a_tensor} and its tensor shape = {a_tensor.shape}\\n')\n",

    "print(f\"A ROW of a_tensor = {a_tensor_row}\\n\")\n",

    "a_tensor_col = a_tensor[:, 2]\n",
    "print(f\"A COL of a_tensor = {a_tensor_col}\\n\")\n",
    "\n",
    "a_tensor_cubic = a_tensor[1:4, 1:4]\n",
    "print(f\"A inner cubic of a_tensor = \\n{a_tensor_cubic}\\n\")\n",

    "# use indexing to extract data that meets some criteria\n",
    "print(\"Extra data > 0.5 = \", a_tensor_cubic > 0.5)\n",
    "print(\"Extra data > 0.5 = \", a_tensor_cubic[a_tensor_cubic > 0.5])"

   "source": [
    "### 4.2 Combining tensors"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": null,
   "metadata": {
    "colab": {
     "base_uri": "https://localhost:8080/"

    "outputId": "70ee5b0d-1611-46c4-fb85-92f552d108e3"
   },
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "a_tensor = torch.tensor([[0,1,2],[3,4,5]])\n",
    "print(f'a_tensor = {a_tensor}\\n')\n",
    "\n",
    "b_tensor = torch.tensor([[10,11,12],[13,14,15]])\n",
    "print(f'b_tensor = {b_tensor}\\n')\n",
    "\n",
    "# using `torch.stack` to add new dimension and stacks -- creates a new dimension\n",
    "stack_tensor_dim0 = torch.stack((a_tensor, b_tensor), dim=0) # stack by rows\n",
    "print(f'stack_tensor_dim0 = \\n{stack_tensor_dim0} and its tensor shape = {stack_tensor_dim0.shape}\\n')\n",
    "\n",
    "stack_tensor_dim1 = torch.stack((a_tensor, b_tensor), dim=1) # stack by columns\n",
    "print(f'stack_tensor_dim1 = \\n{stack_tensor_dim1} and its tensor shape = {stack_tensor_dim1.shape}\\n')\n",
    "\n",
    "# using `torch.cat` to concatenates along existing dim -- extends an existing dimension.\n",
    "cat_tensor_dim0 = torch.cat((a_tensor, b_tensor), dim=0) # cat by rows\n",
    "print(f'cat_tensor_dim0 = \\n{cat_tensor_dim0} and its tensor shape = {cat_tensor_dim0.shape}\\n')\n",
    "\n",
    "cat_tensor_dim1 = torch.cat((a_tensor, b_tensor), dim=1) # cat by columns\n",
    "print(f'cat_tensor_dim1 = \\n{cat_tensor_dim1} and its tensor shape = {cat_tensor_dim1.shape}\\n')"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",

   "source": [
    "### 4.3 Split tensors"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "| Function | Purpose | Input Parameters | Output | Changes Shape | Splits Tensor |\n",
    "| :------: | :-----: | :--------------: | :------: | :------: | :------: |\n",
    "| `torch.chunk` | split into fixed number of chunks | chunks (int), dim | Tuple of tensors | No | Yes |\n",
    "| `torch.split` | split into chunks of specified sizes | split_size_or_sections, dim | Tuple of tensors | No | Yes |\n",
    "| `torch.view` | reshape tensor | New shape | Single tensor | Yes | No |\n",
    "| `torch.unbind` | remove a dimension, split into slices |dim |Tuple of tensors | Yes (removes dim) | Yes |"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": null,
   "metadata": {
    "colab": {
     "base_uri": "https://localhost:8080/"
    },
    "executionInfo": {

    "outputId": "9ae5697d-9e90-4ec6-c958-66724ddc58d1"
   },
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "torch.manual_seed(101)\n",
    "\n",
    "a_tensor = torch.rand(5,5)\n",
    "print(f\"a_tensor = {a_tensor}\\n\")\n",
    "\n",
    "print('--------- torch.unbind(tensor) ---------')\n",
    "tensors = torch.unbind(a_tensor, dim=1)\n",
    "print(f\"first_tensor = {tensors}\")\n",
    "\n",
    "tensors = torch.unbind(a_tensor, dim=0)\n",
    "print(f\"first_tensor = {tensors}\")\n",
    "\n",
    "print('\\n--------- torch.split(tensor) ---------')\n",
    "tensors = torch.split(a_tensor, 3, dim=0) # split by rows\n",
    "print(f\"tensors = {tensors}\\n\")\n",
    "\n",
    "tensors = torch.split(a_tensor, 3, dim=1) # split by cols\n",
    "print(f\"tensors = {tensors}\\n\")"
   ]
  },

   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "# `torch.view` provides an easy way to reshape a tensor\n",
    "\n",
    "a_tensor = torch.randn(9)\n",
    "print(f\"a_tensor = \\n{a_tensor}\\n\")\n",
    "b_tensor = a_tensor.view(3,3)\n",
    "print(f\"b_tensor = \\n{b_tensor}\\n\")\n",
    "\n",
    "# `torch.flatten` method can be used to collapse the dimensions of a given tensor starting with a particular dimension\n",
    "a_tensor = torch.randn(2,3,4)\n",
    "print(f\"a_tensor = \\n{a_tensor}\\n\")\n",
    "b_tensor = torch.flatten(a_tensor, start_dim=0)\n",
    "print(f\"b_tensor = \\n{b_tensor}\\n\")\n",
    "c_tensor = torch.flatten(a_tensor, start_dim=1)\n",
    "print(f\"c_tensor = \\n{c_tensor}\\n\")\n",
    "d_tensor = torch.flatten(a_tensor, start_dim=2)\n",
    "print(f\"d_tensor = \\n{d_tensor}\\n\")\n",
    "\n",
    "print(f\"tensor shapes = b:{b_tensor.shape}\")\n",
    "print(f\"tensor shapes = c:{c_tensor.shape}\")\n",
    "print(f\"tensor shapes = d:{d_tensor.shape}\")"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "<div class='alert alert-info'>\n",
    "\n",
    "Summary ofcommonly used functions to manipulate tensor elements\n",
    "- `torch.cat()`, it concatenates given sequence of tensors in given dimension\n",
    "- `torch.stack()`, it concatenates a sequence of tensors along a new dimension\n",
    "- `torch.chunk()`, it splits a tensor into a specific number of chunks, and each chunk is a view of input tensor\n",
    "- `torch.split()`, it splits tensor into chunks, each chunk is a view or subdivision of original tensor\n",
    "- \n",
    "- `torch.gather(), it gathers values along an axis specified by dimension\n",
    "- `torch.index_select()`, it returns a new tensor that indexes input tensor along a dimension using entries in index, which is a `LongTensor`\n",
    "- `torch.masked_select()`, it returns a new 1D tensor that indexes input tensor according to Boolean mask, which is a `BoolTensor`\n",
    "- `torch.narrow()`, it returns a tensor that is a narrow version of input tensor\n",
    "- `torch.nonzero()`, it returns indices of nonzero elements\n",
    "- `torch.reshape()`, it returns a tensor with same data and number of elements as input tensor, but a different shape, use `view()` instead to ensure tensor is not copied\n",
    "- `torch.squeeze()`, it returns a tensor with all dimensions of input tensor of size 1 removed\n",
    "- `torch.t()`, it expects input to be a 2D tensor and transposes dimensions 0 and 1\n",
    "- `torch.take()`, it returns a tensor at specified indices when\n",
    "slicing is not continuous\n",
    "- `torch.transpose()`, it transposes only specified dimensions\n",
    "- `torch.unbind()`, it removes a tensor dimension by returning a tuple of removed dimension\n",
    "- `torch.unsqueeze()`, it returns a new tensor with a dimension of size 1 inserted at specified position\n",
    "- `torch.where()`, it returns a tensor of selected elements from either one of two tensors, depending on specified condition\n",
    "</div>"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "<div class='alert alert-warning'>\n",
    "\n",
    "Some of these functions may seem redundant, however, following key distinctions and best practices are important to keep in mind\n",
    "- `item()` is an important and commonly used function to return Python number from a tensor containing a single value\n",
    "- use `view()` instead of `reshape()` for reshaping tensors in most cases\n",
    "\t- using `reshape()` may cause tensor to be copied, depending on its layout in memory\n",
    "\t- `view()` ensures that it will not be copied\n",
    "- using `x.T` or `x.t()` is a simple way to transpose 1D or 2D tensors\n",
    "\t- use `transpose()` when dealing with multidimensional tensors\n",
    "- `torch.squeeze()` function is used often in DL to remove an unused dimension\n",
    "\t- *i.e.*, a batch of images with a single image can be reduced from 4D to 3D using `squeeze()`\n",
    "- `torch.unsqueeze()` function is often used in DL to add a dimension of size 1\n",
    "\t- since most PyTorch models expect a batch of data as an input, you could apply `unsqueeze()` when only have one data sample\n",
    "\t- *i.e.*, you can pass a 3D image into `torch.unsqueeze()` to create a batch of one image\n",
    "</div>"
   ]
  },

    "<div class='alert alert-info'>\n",
    "\n",
    "Some commonly used pointwise operations\n",
    "- basic math: `add()`, `div()`, `mul()`, `neg()`, `reciprocal()`, `true_divide()`\n",
    "- truncation: `ceil()`, `clamp()`, `floor()`, `floor_divide()`, `fmod()`, `frac()`, `lerp()`, `remainder()`, `round()`, `sigmoid()`, `trunc()`\n",
    "- complex numbers: `abs()`, `angle()`, `conj()`, `imag()`, `real()`\n",
    "- trigonometry: `acos()`, `asin()`, `atan()`, `cos()`, `cosh()`, `deg2rad()`, `rad2deg()`, `sin()`, `sinh()`, `tan()`, `tanh()`\n",
    "- exponents and logarithms: `exp()`, `expm1()`, `log()`, `log10()`, `log1p()`, `log2()`, `logaddexp()`, `pow()`, `rsqrt()`, `sqrt()`, `square()`\n",
    "- logical: `logical_and()`, `logical_not()`, `logical_or()`, `logical_xor()`\n",
    "- cumulative math: `addcdiv()`, `addcmul()` \n",
    "- bitwise operators: `bitwise_not()`, `bitwise_and()`, `bitwise_or()`, `bitwise_xor()`\n",
    "- error functions: `erf()`, `erfc()`, `erfinv()`\n",
    "- gamma functions: `digamma()`, `lgamma()`, `mvlgamma()`, `polygamma()`\n",
    "</div>"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "<div class='alert alert-warning'>\n",
    "\n",
    "Note that three different syntaxes can be used for most tensor operations\n",
    "- tensors support operator overloading, so you can use operators directly, as in `z = x + y`\n",
    "- although you can also use PyTorch functions such as `torch.add()` to do same thing, this is less common\n",
    "- lastly, you can perform in-place operations using underscore (_) postfix\n",
    "\t- function `y.add_(x)` achieves same results, but they’ll be stored in y\n",
    "</div>"
   ]
  },

  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "<div class='alert alert-info'>\n",
    "\n",
    "Summary of some commonly used reduction operations\n",
    "- `torch.argmax(input, dim, keepdim=False, out=None)`, it returns index(es) of maximum value across all elements, or just a dimension if it’s specified\n",
    "    - `torch.argmin(input, dim, keepdim=False, out=None)`, it returns index(es) of minimum value across all elements, or just a dimension if it’s specified\n",
    "- `torch.dist(input, dim, keepdim=False, out=None)`, it computes p-norm of two tensors\n",
    "- `torch.logsumexp(input, dim, keepdim=False, out=None)`, it computes log of summed exponentials of each row of input tensor in given dimension\n",
    "- `torch.mean(input, dim, keepdim=False, out=None)`, it computes mean or average across all elements, or just a dimension if it’s specified\n",
    "    - `torch.median(input, dim, keepdim=False, out=None)`, it computes median or middle value across all elements, or just a dimension if it’s specified\n",
    "    - `torch.mode(input, dim, keepdim=False, out=None)`, it computes mode or most frequent value across all elements, or just a dimension if it’s specified\n",
    "- `torch.norm(input, p='fro', dim=None, keepdim=False, out=None, dtype=None)`, it computes matrix or vector norm across all elements, or just a dimension if it’s specified\n",
    "- `torch.prod(input, dim, keepdim=False, dtype=None)`, it computes product of all elements, or of each row of input tensor if it’s specified\n",
    "- `torch.std(input, dim, keepdim=False, out=None)`, it computes standard deviation across all elements, or just a dimension if it’s specified\n",
    "    - `torch.std_mean(input, unbiased=True)`, it computes standard deviation and mean across all elements, or just a dimension if it’s specified\n",
    "- `torch.sum(input, dim, keepdim=False, out=None)`, it computes sum of all elements, or just a dimension if it’s specified\n",
    "- `torch.unique(input, dim, keepdim=False, out=None)`, it removes duplicates across entire tensor, or just a dimension if it’s specified\n",
    "\t- `torch.unique_consecutive(input, dim, keepdim=False, out=None)`, it is similar to `torch.unique()` but only removes consecutive duplicates\n",
    "- `torch.var(input, dim, keepdim=False, out=None)`, it computes variance across all elements, or just a dimension if it’s specified\n",
    "\t- `torch.var_mean(input, dim, keepdim=False, out=None)`, it computes mean and variance across all elements, or just a dimension if it’s specified\n",
    "</div>"
   ]
  },

   "source": [
    "torch.manual_seed(123456)\n",
    "\n",
    "a_tensor = torch.rand(2,3)\n",
    "b_tensor = torch.rand(2,3)\n",
    "print(f\"a_tensor = \\n{a_tensor}\\n\")\n",
    "print(f\"b_tensor = \\n{b_tensor}\\n\")\n",
    "\n",
    "ge_torch = torch.ge(a_tensor, b_tensor).long()\n",
    "print(f\"ge_torch = \\n{ge_torch}\\n\")\n",
    "\n",
    "lt_torch = torch.lt(a_tensor, b_tensor).long()\n",
    "print(f\"lt_torch = \\n{lt_torch}\\n\")\n",
    "\n",
    "# torch.le(), torch.eq(), torch.ne()"
   ]

  {

   "source": [
    "# `any` and `all` methods enable to check whether a given condition is true in any or all cases\n",
    "\n",
    "a_tensor = torch.randn(3,3)\n",
    "print(f\"Tensor A = {a_tensor}\\n\")\n",
    "\n",
    "print(torch.any(a > 0.0).long())\n",
    "print(torch.any(a > 1.0))\n",
    "print(torch.all(a > 0.0))\n",
    "print(torch.all(a > 1.0))"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "<div class='alert alert-info'>\n",
    "\n",
    "Comparison functions seem pretty straightforward, common pitfalls include following\n",
    "- `torch.eq()` function or `==` returns a tensor of same size with a Boolean result for each element\n",
    "\t- `torch.equal()` function tests if tensors are same size, and if all elements within tensor are equal then it returns a single Boolean value\n",
    "- `torch.allclose()` also returns a single Boolean value if all elements are close to a specified value\n",
    "</div>"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {
    "id": "6q6FycDe-Ywx"
   },
   "source": [
    "#### 4.4.4 Linear algebra operations"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "Linear algebra functions facilitate matrix operations and are important for DL computations\n",
    "- enable matrix operations and are essential for DL computations\n",
    "- functions for matrix computations and tensor computations\n",
    "- PyTorch has a module called `torch.linalg` than contains a set of build-in functions that are based on BLAS and LAPACK standardized libraries"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": null,
   "metadata": {
    "colab": {
     "base_uri": "https://localhost:8080/"
    },
    "executionInfo": {
     "elapsed": 14,
     "status": "ok",
     "timestamp": 1749255470713,
     "user": {
      "displayName": "Yonglei Wang",
      "userId": "00334589855046956617"
     },
     "user_tz": -120
    },
    "id": "_okk-hLHAtrv",
    "outputId": "0be8232a-c862-4886-d1f0-7be0d69484ff"
   },
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "# compute dot product (scalar) of two 1D tensors\n",
    "a_tensor = torch.tensor([1, 2, 3, 4], dtype=torch.int32)\n",
    "b_tensor = torch.tensor(np.arange(1,9,2), dtype=torch.int32)\n",
    "\n",
    "ab_tensor = torch.matmul(a_tensor, b_tensor)\n",
    "print(f\"Torch.matmul for two 1D scalarss = {ab_tensor}\")\n",
    "\n",
    "# compute matrix-matrix product (2D tensor) of two 2D tensors\n",
    "a_tensor = torch.tensor([[1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6]])\n",
    "b_tensor = torch.tensor([[1, 2], [3, 4], [5, 6]])\n",
    "\n",
    "ab_tensor = torch.matmul(a_tensor, b_tensor)\n",
    "print(f\"Torch.matmul for two 2D matrices = {ab_tensor}\\n\")"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": null,
   "metadata": {
    "colab": {
     "base_uri": "https://localhost:8080/"
    },
    "executionInfo": {
     "elapsed": 17,
     "status": "ok",
     "timestamp": 1749255470731,
     "user": {
      "displayName": "Yonglei Wang",
      "userId": "00334589855046956617"
     },
     "user_tz": -120
    },
    "id": "GVMQ0Pe91Wh5",
    "outputId": "88bc83e6-5cd8-4b0d-b577-37899e5bd47d"
   },
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "# compute a matrix product of multiple 2D tensors\n",
    "\n",
    "a_tensor = torch.rand(2, 3)\n",
    "b_tensor = torch.rand(3, 4)\n",
    "c_tensor = torch.rand(4, 5)\n",
    "d_tensor = torch.rand(5, 6)\n",
    "abcd_tensor = torch.matmul(torch.matmul(a_tensor, b_tensor), torch.matmul(c_tensor, d_tensor))\n",
    "print(f\"Torch.matmul for four 2D matrices = \\n{abcd_tensor}\")\n",
    "\n",
    "abcd_tensor = torch.linalg.multi_dot((a_tensor, b_tensor, c_tensor, d_tensor))\n",
    "print(f\"Torch.linalg.multi_dot for four 2D matrices = \\n{abcd_tensor}\")"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": null,
   "metadata": {
    "colab": {
     "base_uri": "https://localhost:8080/"
    },
    "executionInfo": {
     "elapsed": 26,
     "status": "ok",
     "timestamp": 1749255470804,
     "user": {
      "displayName": "Yonglei Wang",
      "userId": "00334589855046956617"
     },
     "user_tz": -120
    },
    "id": "MQ0JaFNA1Xzh",
    "outputId": "e2e508f2-d4e2-4585-c360-96174de38cd5"
   },
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "# compute eigenvalues and eigenvectors\n",
    "\n",
    "a_tensor = torch.rand(4,4)\n",
    "\n",
    "print(f\"Tensor A = {a_tensor}\\n\")\n",
    "\n",
    "eigenvalues, eigenvectors = torch.linalg.eigh(a_tensor)\n",
    "print(f\"Eigenvalues = {eigenvalues}\\n\")\n",
    "print(f\"Eigenvectors = {eigenvectors}\")"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "<div class='alert alert-info'>\n",
    "\n",
    "Summary of some commonly used linear algebra operations\n",
    "- `torch.matmul()`, it computes a matrix product of two tensors; supports broadcasting\n",
    "- `torch.chain_matmul()`, it computes a matrix product of N tensors\n",
    "- `torch.mm()`, it computes a matrix product of two tensors (if broadcasting is required, use `matmul()`)\n",
    "- `torch.addmm()`, it computes a matrix product of two tensors and adds it to input\n",
    "- `torch.bmm()`, it computes a batch of matrix products\n",
    "- `torch.addbmm()`, it computes a batch of matrix products and adds it to input\n",
    "- `torch.baddbmm()`, it computes a batch of matrix products and adds it to input batch\n",
    "- `torch.mv()`, it computes product of matrix and vector\n",
    "- `torch.addmv()`, it computes product of matrix and vector and adds it to input\n",
    "- `torch.matrix_power`, it returns a tensor raised to power of n (for square\n",
    "tensors)\n",
    "- `torch.eig()`, it finds eigenvalues and eigenvectors of a real square tensor\n",
    "- `torch.inverse()`, it computes inverse of a square tensor\n",
    "- `torch.det()`, it computes determinant of a matrix or batch of matrices\n",
    "- `torch.logdet()`, it computes log determinant of a matrix or batch of matrices\n",
    "- `torch.dot()`, it computes inner product of two tensors\n",
    "- `torch.addr()`, it computes outer product of two tensors and adds it to input\n",
    "- `torch.solve()`, it returns solution to a system of linear equations\n",
    "- `torch.svd()`, it performs a single-value decomposition\n",
    "- `torch.pca_lowrank()`, it performs a linear principle component analysis\n",
    "- `torch.cholesky()`, it computes a Cholesky decomposition\n",
    "- `torch.cholesky_inverse()`, it computes inverse of a symmetric positive definite matrix and returns Cholesky factor\n",
    "- `torch.cholesky_solve()`, it solves a system of linear equations using Cholesky factor\n",
    "</div>"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "### 4.5 Activation functions & Automatic differentiation"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",

    "id": "Yo72y7ufULIS"
   },
   "source": [
    "#### 4.5.1 Activation functions"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": null,
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "image = Image.open(\"./images/data/activation-function.png\")\n",

    "plt.show()"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": null,
   "metadata": {
    "colab": {
     "base_uri": "https://localhost:8080/"
    },
    "executionInfo": {
     "elapsed": 57,
     "status": "ok",
     "timestamp": 1749255471015,
     "user": {
      "displayName": "Yonglei Wang",
      "userId": "00334589855046956617"
     },
     "user_tz": -120
    },
    "id": "aCKpGJS1USC6",
    "outputId": "dd1dc422-481b-40e7-f392-d07528ea464e"
   },
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "a_tensor  = torch.linspace(-1.0, 1.0, steps=15)\n",
    "print(f\"a_tensor = {a_tensor}\\n\")\n",
    "\n",
    "# linear activation = identity\n",
    "print(f\"using linear  function = {a_tensor}\")\n",
    "print(f\"using sigmoid function = {torch.sigmoid(a_tensor)}]\")\n",
    "print(f\"using tanh    function = {torch.tanh(a_tensor)}]\")\n",

   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "#### 4.5.2 Automatic differentiation (Autograd)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "One function, `backward()`, is worth calling out in its own subsection because it’s what makes PyTorch so powerful for DL development\n",
    "- `backward()` function uses PyTorch’s automatic differentiation package, `torch.autograd`, to differentiate and compute gradients of tensors based on chain rule\n",
    "- here’s a simple example of autodifferentiation\n",
    "\t- we define a function, `f = sum(x2)`, where $x$ is a matrix of variables\n",
    "\t- if we want to find $\\frac{df}{dx}$ for each variable in matrix, we need to set `requires_grad = True` flag for tensor $x$\n",
    "- `f.backward()` function performs differentiation with respect to $f$ and stores $\\frac{df}{dx}$ in `x.grad` attribute\n",
    "\t- a quick review of calculus differential equations will tell us the derivation of $f$ with respect to $x$, $\\frac{df}{dx}=2x$\n",
    "\t- results of evaluating $\\frac{df}{dx}$ for values of $x$ are shown as output\n",
    "- **only tensors of floating-point dtype can require gradients**"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": null,
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "x = torch.tensor([[1,2,3],[4,5,6]], dtype=torch.float, requires_grad=True)\n",
    "print(x)\n",
    "\n",
    "f = x.pow(2).sum()\n",
    "print(f)\n",
    "\n",
    "f.backward()\n",
    "print(x.grad) # df/dx = 2x"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",

   "source": [
    "### 5.1 Tensor.device (CPU vs CUDA)\n"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": null,
   "metadata": {
    "colab": {
     "base_uri": "https://localhost:8080/"
    },
    "executionInfo": {
     "elapsed": 656,
     "status": "ok",

     "user": {

    },

   },
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "a_tensor = torch.rand(3,4) # 'cpu by default'\n",
    "print(f'a_tensor = {a_tensor} and its tensor device = {a_tensor.device}\\n')\n",
    "\n",

    "a_tensor = torch.rand(3,4, device='cuda') # cuda for gpu, there is no error if you have GPU\n",

  },
  {

  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "### 5.2 Moving tensors between CPUs and GPUs"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {
    "id": "f1p2_dZsHppi"
   },
   "source": [
    "**Moving Tensors between CPUs and GPUs**\n",
    "- Transfer data from CPU to GPU\n",
    "- After training, output Tensors are produced in GPU\n",
    "- Output data requires preprocessing\n",
    "- Some  preprocessing libraries don't support Tensors and expect a Numpy array\n",
    "- Numpy supports only data in GPU, and we need to move data from GPU to CPU"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": null,
   "metadata": {
    "colab": {
     "base_uri": "https://localhost:8080/"
    },
    "executionInfo": {
     "elapsed": 6,
     "status": "ok",
     "timestamp": 1749255470302,
     "user": {
      "displayName": "Yonglei Wang",
      "userId": "00334589855046956617"
     },
     "user_tz": -120
    },
    "id": "soJaJiBpHppi",
    "outputId": "53244cf6-034a-473f-a6d4-f97eb2288256"
   },
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "# data from CPU to GPU --- 3 methods\n",
    "\n",
    "a_tensor = torch.rand((2,4), device='cpu')\n",
    "print(f'a_tensor = {a_tensor} and its tensor device = {a_tensor.device}\\n')\n",
    "\n",
    "# 1. `Tensor.cuda()`\n",
    "b_tensor = a_tensor.cuda()\n",
    "print(f'b_tensor = {b_tensor} and its tensor device = {b_tensor.device}\\n')\n",
    "\n",
    "# 2. `Tensor.to(\"cuda\")`\n",
    "b_tensor = a_tensor.to(\"cuda\")\n",
    "print(f'b_tensor = {b_tensor} and its tensor device = {b_tensor.device}\\n')\n",
    "\n",
    "# 3. `Tensor.to(\"cuda:0\")`\n",
    "b_tensor = a_tensor.to(\"cuda:0\")\n",
    "print(f'b_tensor = {b_tensor} and its tensor device = {b_tensor.device}\\n')"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": null,
   "metadata": {
    "colab": {
     "base_uri": "https://localhost:8080/"
    },
    "executionInfo": {
     "elapsed": 77,
     "status": "ok",
     "timestamp": 1749255470381,
     "user": {
      "displayName": "Yonglei Wang",
      "userId": "00334589855046956617"
     },
     "user_tz": -120
    },
    "id": "IbV-PiVHHppi",
    "outputId": "14da693c-47c2-4f64-fa2f-6149a2af1c5e"
   },
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "# data from GPU to CPU --- 2 methods\n",
    "\n",
    "a_tensor = torch.rand((4), requires_grad=True, device='cuda')\n",
    "print(f'a_tensor = {a_tensor} and its tensor device = {a_tensor.device}\\n')\n",
    "\n",
    "# 1. `Tensor.cpu()` with `requires_grad=False`\n",
    "b_tensor = a_tensor.cpu()\n",
    "print(f'b_tensor = {b_tensor} and its tensor device = {b_tensor.device}\\n')\n",
    "\n",
    "# 2. `Tensor.detach().cpu() with `requires_grad=True`\n",
    "b_tensor = a_tensor.detach().cpu()\n",
    "print(f'b_tensor = {b_tensor} and its tensor device = {b_tensor.device}\\n')"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": null,
   "metadata": {
    "colab": {
     "base_uri": "https://localhost:8080/"
    },
    "executionInfo": {
     "elapsed": 20,
     "status": "ok",
     "timestamp": 1749255569561,
     "user": {
      "displayName": "Yonglei Wang",
      "userId": "00334589855046956617"
     },
     "user_tz": -120
    },
    "id": "EVlgrmyXHppi",
    "outputId": "54b26d8e-e30c-4a4a-ab71-8aaf67aca5ce"
   },
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "# gpu tensor -> cpu tensor -> cpu numpy array -> cpu tensor --> gpu tensor\n",
    "\n",
    "# generate a tensor on GPU\n",
    "a_tensor_gpu = torch.rand((2,2), requires_grad=True, device='cuda')\n",
    "print(f'a_tensor_gpu = {a_tensor_gpu} and its tensor device = {a_tensor_gpu.device}\\n')\n",
    "\n",
    "# transfer tensor (it is still a tensor!) from GPU to CPU\n",
    "a_tensor_cpu = a_tensor_gpu.detach().cpu()\n",
    "print(f'a_tensor_cpu = {a_tensor_cpu} and its array device = {a_tensor_cpu.device}\\n')\n",
    "\n",
    "# convert CPU tensor to Numpy array (it is not a tensor)\n",
    "a_array_from_tensor = a_tensor_cpu.numpy()\n",
    "print(f'a_array_from_tensor = {a_array_from_tensor}\\n') # it is not a tensor and Numpy doesnot have a `device` attribute\n",
    "\n",
    "# convert numpy array to tensor (CPU) again \n",
    "a_tensor_from_array = torch.from_numpy(a_array_from_tensor)\n",
    "print(f'a_tensor_from_array = {a_tensor_from_array} and its tensor device = {a_tensor_from_array.device}\\n')"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## 6. Conversion Images to Tensors"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "### 6.1 Grayscale images"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "The [MNIST dataset (Modified National Institute of Standards and Technology)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MNIST_database) is one of the most widely used datasets in machine learning and computer vision.\n",
    "- It was created in 1998 by Yann LeCun and collaborators as a simplified benchmark for handwritten digit recognition tasks.\n",
    "- It contains a total of 70000 grayscale images of handwritten digits ranging from 0 to 9, and each image is a 28 × 28 pixel square, giving 784 features when flattened into a vector."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": null,
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "from sklearn.datasets import fetch_openml\n",
    "\n",
    "# download MNIST from OpenML\n",
    "mnist = fetch_openml('mnist_784', version=1, as_frame=False)\n",
    "\n",
    "# features (images) and labels\n",
    "X, y = mnist.data, mnist.target\n",
    "\n",
    "print(\"Images shape:\", X.shape)   # (70000, 784)\n",
    "print(X[1]) # 874 = 28 * 28"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": null,
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "# show second image\n",
    "plt.imshow(X[1].reshape(28, 28), cmap=\"gray\")\n",
    "plt.title(f\"Label: {y[1]}\")\n",
    "plt.show()"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": null,
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "print(\"Labels shape:\", y.shape)   # (70000,)\n",
    "print(\"Label classes:\", set(y))"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "### 6.2 Color images"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "In computer vision, color images are typically represented using three channels corresponding to **Red**, **Green**, and **Blue** (RGB).\n",
    "- Each channel captures the intensity of one color component for every pixel in the image.\n",
    "- Converting a color image into a three-channel tensor ensures that these separate color intensities are preserved, allowing machine learning models to extract meaningful features from the combination of colors."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "<div class='alert alert-warning'>\n",
    "\n",
    ":::{warning}\n",
    "Deep learning frameworks, such as PyTorch and TensorFlow, expect input images in a channel-first or channel-last tensor format.\n",
    "- PyTorch follows the channel-first (C, H, W) convention because it maps well to how CUDA/cuDNN kernels expect data for convolution operations.\n",
    "- TensorFlow/Keras defaults to channel-last (H, W, C) because it’s more natural for humans (rows × columns × colors), and it aligns with NumPy and most image processing libraries.\n",
    ":::\n",
    "</div>"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": null,
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "# load a color image (replace with your image path)\n",
    "image_path = \"./1-berzelius.jpg\"\n",
    "image = Image.open(image_path).convert(\"RGB\")  # ensure 3 channels\n",
    "\n",
    "# show the original image\n",
    "plt.imshow(image)\n",
    "plt.axis(\"off\")\n",

    "\n",
    "# convert image to tensor\n",
    "transform = transforms.ToTensor()\n",
    "tensor_image = transform(image)  # shape in (C, H, W)\n",
    "\n",
    "# print tensor size\n",
    "print(\"Tensor shape:\", tensor_image.shape)  # (3, H, W) means 3 channels\n",
    "print(f\"Min value: {tensor_image.min().item()} and Max value: {tensor_image.max().item()}\")\n",
    "\n",
    "print('\\n', tensor_image)"
   ]

    "# split into three separate channels\n",
    "red_channel = tensor_image[0:1, :, :]    # shape: (1, H, W)\n",

    "blue_channel = tensor_image[2:3, :, :]   # shape: (1, H, W)"
   ]

    "axes[0].set_title(\"Red Channel\")\n",
